raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ### What does this PR do? Add end-to-end native NVFP4 W4A4 training and rollout on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, demonstrated with Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base DAPO using Megatron/Transformer Engine and vLLM. This contributes to Sophia's [low-precision roadmap #5972](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/5972), specifically **NVFP4 real quant** and **NVFP4 training in Megatron**. In brief: - **Training:** Transformer Engine runs selected routed-expert MLPs in NVFP4 with per-token activation scaling and dequantized backward. Persistent policy weights remain BF16, with full optimizer state. - **Weight synchronization:** transfer BF16 weights after each policy update. - **Rollout:** vLLM quantizes and packs expert weights during native reload, then uses NVFP4 weights and dynamic per-token activation scaling for generation. Refit preserves the storage referenced by CUDA graphs. Attention and the configured boundary-layer MLPs remain BF16. The Qwen3 example keeps the first two and last four MLP layers in BF16 and applies NVFP4 to the remaining 42 routed-expert MLP layers. ### Checklist Before Starting - [x] Search for similar PRs: [NVFP4](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+NVFP4), [roadmap #5972](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+5972+in%3Abody). - [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`. Related work: #6455 targets ModelOpt/TRT-LLM synchronization; #6992 provides FSDP W4A8 simulation; #7895 targets DeepSeek MXFP4 on TE FP8; #7519 adds MXFP8 training and rollout. This PR adds native TE NVFP4 training with per-token vLLM NVFP4 rollout and repeated online refit. ### Test Unit tests (CPU and GB200) pass; scoped Ruff, formatting and lockfile checks pass. #### Long run BF16 and W4A4 runs of the example script below (Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base, DAPO, R3, token-level TIS) on 8 nodes × 4 GB200 GPUs, 700 steps with checkpoint resume across jobs. **W4A4 vs BF16:** **Training score (`critic/score/mean`)** **Entropy (`actor/entropy`)** **Train–rollout mismatch (`rollout_corr/kl`)** **Gradient norm (`actor/grad_norm`)** **Performance:** at matched response length, NVFP4 rollout generation is about 1.3× faster than BF16 once the mean response exceeds ~2.5k tokens, giving roughly 1.2× shorter end-to-end steps; NVFP4 training itself is still slower than BF16 in Transformer Engine. ### API and Usage Example With a Ray cluster running on eight nodes, provide model and dataset paths shared by all workers: ```bash MODEL_PATH=/shared/models/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base \ TRAIN_FILE=/shared/data/train.parquet \ TEST_FILE=/shared/data/validation.parquet \ EXP_NAME=qwen3-native-nvfp4 \ PRECISION_MODE=real_nvfp4 \ bash examples/real_nvfp4/run_qwen3_30b_megatron.sh ``` Use `PRECISION_MODE=bf16` for the baseline. NVFP4 is enabled through `actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.real_nvfp4`: `enable`, `backward_override`, and `num_layers_at_start_in_bf16` / `num_layers_at_end_in_bf16`, which keep whole decoder layers BF16 in both training and rollout. The example uses the standard verl PPO entry point, parquet datasets and built-in reward manager, with the DAPO recipe (clip-higher, token-level loss, dynamic sampling and the overlong penalty), R3 routing replay and token-level TIS. See [the example guide](https://github.com/zhangyimi/verl/blob/feat/native-nvfp4/examples/real_nvfp4/README.md) for configuration and runtime setup. ### Design & Code Changes - **Training precision:** the Megatron per-module recipe (attention BF16, routed-expert MLPs NVFP4, carved-out layers BF16) is generated from the configuration rather than maintained as a file. After model construction, the effective precision of every attention and expert linear layer is checked against it. Packed THD sequences use the TE alignment for FP4 as for FP8. - **Native refit:** load the BF16 weights through vLLM's layerwise reload, which quantizes each complete expert layer. The refit checks expert-weight coverage, and the packed-weight and scale storage is preserved across refits and sleep/wake cycles. The legacy MoE weight-loader patch is skipped only on this path. - **Routing replay:** use vLLM’s native fused-MoE routing capture and align replay data with FP4 training padding. - **Runtime compatibility:** align the CUDA 13 stack and apply the vLLM 0.29 NVFP4 refit-scale compatibility patch during environment setup. Upstream [vLLM #57954](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57954), included in 0.31, fixes the stale weight-scale portion; reciprocal activation-scale storage still needs restoration across level-2 sleep/wake. The validated Megatron + vLLM stack uses: | Component | Version | |---|---| | PyTorch | 2.13 / CUDA 13 | | vLLM | 0.29.0 | | Transformers | 5.12.1 | | Megatron-Core | 0.19.2 | | Megatron-Bridge | 0.6.2 | | Transformer Engine | 2.18.0 | | FlashInfer | 0.6.18 | | CUTLASS DSL / QuACK | 4.6.2 / 0.6.4 | SGLang end-to-end validation remains follow-up work. ### Checklist Before Submitting - [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Run the complete all-files pre-commit suite. +# vLLM NVFP4 compatibility patch once, at image build time. The default image

+# Native NVFP4 training and rollout
+
+This example trains Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base with Megatron/Transformer Engine and
+runs vLLM rollout using native NVFP4 weights and per-token activation scaling.
+Persistent training weights and actor-to-rollout transfers remain BF16.
+vLLM packs the transferred weights during native reload, preserving the storage
+used by CUDA graphs across policy updates.
+
+## Precision and supported configuration
+
+Setting `actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.real_nvfp4.enable=True` runs the
+routed-expert MLPs in NVFP4 with per-token activation scaling, dequantized
+backward, and adaptive 4-over-6 disabled. Attention, router, norms,
+embeddings and the LM head remain BF16. `num_layers_at_start_in_bf16` and
+`num_layers_at_end_in_bf16` keep whole decoder layers in BF16 for both training
+and rollout; this example keeps the first two and last four.
+
+The current integration supports the all-MoE `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` layout,
+training PP=1 without virtual pipeline parallelism, and rollout TP/PP/EP=1/1/1.
+It uses BF16 KV cache, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` CUDA graphs and no speculative decoding.
+Mixed dense/MoE layouts and shared experts are not supported.
+
+## Installation
+
+The runtime uses PyTorch 2.13.0/CUDA 13, Transformer Engine 2.18.0,

+def test_native_packing_matches_per_expert_gpu_reference(dtype, strided):
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(17029)
+    weight = torch.randn((4, 64, 128), device="cuda", dtype=dtype, generator=generator)

+    scale = (6.0 * 448.0) / weight.abs().amax(dim=(1, 2)).float().clamp_min(1e-8)
+    reference = [

+        for w, s in zip(weight, scale, strict=True)

+"""Validation for routed-expert, per-token NVFP4 training and rollout."""
+
+from typing import Any
+
+
+def _hf_get(hf_config: Any, name: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
+    if isinstance(hf_config, dict):
+        return hf_config.get(name, default)
+    return getattr(hf_config, name, default)
+
+
+def real_nvfp4_moe_layer_indices(hf_config: Any) -> list[int]:
+    """Indices of the decoder layers that carry routed experts.
+
+    Derived from the config rather than from the architecture name, following
+    the HF placement rule shared by the Qwen MoE family: layer ``i`` is sparse
+    when it is not listed in ``mlp_only_layers`` and ``(i + 1)`` is a multiple
+    of ``decoder_sparse_step``. Models that omit those keys are all-MoE.
+    """
+
+    num_layers = int(_hf_get(hf_config, "num_hidden_layers") or 0)
+    sparse_step = int(_hf_get(hf_config, "decoder_sparse_step") or 1)
+    dense_layers = set(_hf_get(hf_config, "mlp_only_layers") or [])
+    if sparse_step <= 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"real_nvfp4 needs a positive decoder_sparse_step, got {sparse_step}")
+    return [i for i in range(num_layers) if i not in dense_layers and (i + 1) % sparse_step == 0]
+
+
+def real_nvfp4_bf16_layer_indices(num_layers: int, num_layers_at_start: int, num_layers_at_end: int) -> list[int]:
+    """Decoder layers kept in BF16 by the first/last carve-out."""
+
+    if num_layers_at_start < 0 or num_layers_at_end < 0:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"real_nvfp4 BF16 layer carve-out must be non-negative, got {num_layers_at_start}/{num_layers_at_end}"
+        )
+    if num_layers_at_start + num_layers_at_end >= num_layers:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"real_nvfp4 BF16 layer carve-out {num_layers_at_start}/{num_layers_at_end} "
+            f"leaves no quantized layer of {num_layers}"
+        )
+    return list(range(num_layers_at_start)) + list(range(num_layers - num_layers_at_end, num_layers))
+
+
+def real_nvfp4_moe_layer_partition(
+    hf_config: Any,
+    *,
+    num_layers_at_start_in_bf16: int = 0,
+    num_layers_at_end_in_bf16: int = 0,
+) -> tuple[list[int], list[int]]:
+    """Return routed-expert layer indices as ``(quantized, bf16)``."""
+
+    num_layers = int(_hf_get(hf_config, "num_hidden_layers") or 0)
+    carved = set(real_nvfp4_bf16_layer_indices(num_layers, num_layers_at_start_in_bf16, num_layers_at_end_in_bf16))
+    moe_layers = real_nvfp4_moe_layer_indices(hf_config)
+    return [i for i in moe_layers if i not in carved], [i for i in moe_layers if i in carved]
+
+
+def real_nvfp4_vllm_ignore_layers(
+    hf_config: Any,
+    *,
+    num_layers_at_start_in_bf16: int = 0,
+    num_layers_at_end_in_bf16: int = 0,
+) -> list[str]:
+    """Exact vLLM module names excluded from online NVFP4."""
+
+    _, bf16_moe_layers = real_nvfp4_moe_layer_partition(
+        hf_config,
+        num_layers_at_start_in_bf16=num_layers_at_start_in_bf16,
+        num_layers_at_end_in_bf16=num_layers_at_end_in_bf16,
+    )
+    return [f"model.layers.{index}.mlp.experts" for index in bf16_moe_layers]
+
+
+def real_nvfp4_quant_recipe_config(num_layers: int, num_layers_at_start: int, num_layers_at_end: int) -> dict:
+    """Megatron-Core per-module recipe: attention BF16, routed-expert MLP NVFP4.
+
+    The result is passed to ``RecipeConfig.from_config_dict``. MCore takes the
+    first matching matcher, so the carved-out layers precede the general MLP
+    patterns. Layer indices in module paths are global only with PP=1, which
+    :func:`validate_real_nvfp4_parallelism` enforces.
+    """
+
+    def glob(config: str, pattern: str) -> dict:
+        return {"config": config, "type": "glob", "pattern": pattern, "enabled": True}
+
+    matchers = {
+        f"layer_{index}_bf16": glob("bf16", f"*.layers.{index}.*")
+        for index in real_nvfp4_bf16_layer_indices(num_layers, num_layers_at_start, num_layers_at_end)
+    }
+    matchers["attn_qkv_bf16"] = glob("bf16", "*.linear_qkv")
+    matchers["attn_proj_bf16"] = glob("bf16", "*.linear_proj")
+    matchers["mlp_fc1_nvfp4"] = glob("nvfp4", "*.linear_fc1")
+    matchers["mlp_fc2_nvfp4"] = glob("nvfp4", "*.linear_fc2")
+    return {
+        "configs": {
+            "bf16": {"transformer_engine_config_type": "TEQuantizationParams", "training_recipe": {}},
+            "nvfp4": {
+                "transformer_engine_config_type": "TEQuantizationParams",
+                "training_recipe": {"fp4_quantization_recipe": "nvfp4"},
+            },
+        },
+        "matchers": matchers,
+    }
+
+

+    """Restrict the current recipe to all-MoE decoders without shared experts.
+
+    The training recipe's fc1/fc2 patterns would also quantize dense MLPs,

+    stay unsupported until non-expert precision is configured on both sides.
+    """

+    num_experts = int(_hf_get(hf_config, "num_experts") or _hf_get(hf_config, "n_routed_experts") or 0)

+        raise ValueError(
+            "real_nvfp4 requires a routed-expert MoE model; this config declares no experts "
+            "(looked for num_experts / n_routed_experts)"
+        )
+    num_layers = int(_hf_get(hf_config, "num_hidden_layers") or 0)

+            "real_nvfp4 currently requires every decoder layer to be MoE; mixed dense/MoE layouts "
+            "would quantize dense training MLPs that remain BF16 in rollout"

+    # Shared experts would be extra per-layer weights on the refit stream, so the

+    for key in ("n_shared_experts", "shared_expert_intermediate_size", "num_shared_experts"):
+        if int(_hf_get(hf_config, key) or 0) > 0:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"real_nvfp4 does not model shared experts yet ({key}="
